matches.note: The eclipse of the moon as a portent of disaster before which people seek protection. Akkadian an-na-a ša a-na {d}30 ina AN.GE₆ iz-za-mi-ir, with laments and the brazier 'until the eclipse clears' (a-di AN.GE₆ u-nam-mar), mourners with covered heads, and the refrain that confinement, murder, rebellion and the eclipse not come near Uruk. Arabic wa-khasafa l-qamar among the signs of the Day; man says ayna l-mafarr, answered kallā lā wazar. A recurring, ritually averted omen in Uruk; a single final sign with no averting in 75:8-11.

Only in Lunar eclipse ritual at Uruk: the kalû's lament ('the Dilmunite whose ship sank am I'), the brazier, kispu, mourners with covered heads (BRM 4, 6 obverse): During a lunar eclipse a brazier is lit at the temple gates and the lamentation priest performs laments until the moon becomes bright again; In a lament the god (or his mourner) says: I am the one who roams and does not sleep, who ate no food and drank no water in his weariness; Mourners smear their faces, hands and feet with river mud and hang a dagger at the collarbone; Lament: I am the Dilmunite whose ship sank in the reed thicket; Prayer refrain: may confinement, murder, rebellion and (the evil of) the eclipse not come near the city and its temples; Destruction is ascribed to 'the word of An and the word of Enlil', to the angry heart of the high gods; The altar fire must burn continually and never go out; A disgraced man goes home mourning with his head covered; A funerary offering (kispu) is made to the netherworld gods (Anunnaki) within a royal rite; After the rite the remains (brazier and ashes, magic circle, twine, purification materials) are thrown into the river; In the ruined temple the offerings, festivals, songs, drums and priestly offices cease.

Only in Judgment of the nations in the Valley of Jehoshaphat; the fountain from the temple: The nations cast lots for God's people, trading a boy for a harlot and a girl for wine; Put in the sickle, the harvest is ripe; the winepress is full and the vats overflow with wickedness; Tyre, Sidon and Philistia sold Judeans to the Ionians (Greeks); Measure for measure: the slave-traders' children will be sold to the Sabeans; Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision (emeq he-harus); Beat your plowshares into swords and pruning hooks into spears (call to war); A spring issues from the house of YHWH and waters the Wadi of Shittim (Acacias); Jerusalem will be holy and strangers will pass through it no more; God gathers all nations to the Valley of Jehoshaphat ('YHWH judges') to judge them; YHWH roars from Zion and utters his voice from Jerusalem; heaven and earth shake; A river flows from under the temple threshold, growing ever deeper; On the day the sky heaves (tamur) and the mountains move away; and 1 more.

Only in The resurrection: bones, fingertips and the collarbone: On that day radiant faces look upon their Lord (beatific vision); Does man think he will be left aimless (suda), without purpose or accountability?; Oath by the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwama); At death the soul reaches the collarbones, someone asks 'who is a healer (or charmer, raq)?', leg is wrapped with leg and the drive is to the Lord; The prophet is told not to hasten with the recitation before its revelation is complete; The body of the dead is made whole again, all its limbs complete [divergence between the texts]; An eclipse of the moon as a portent of disaster before which people seek escape or protection [divergence between the texts]; Man will be evidence against himself, even if he offers his excuses; At the prophet's word there is a rattling; bones come together bone to bone, then sinews, flesh and skin cover them, but there is no breath; Then each soul will know what it has brought forward and what it left behind; On that day man asks 'where to flee?' but there is no refuge; the destination is with God; God created humans (and things) in pairs, male and female; and 6 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: On that day man asks 'where to flee?' but there is no refuge; the destination is with God (weight 7.3); God poured the embryo out like milk and curdled it like cheese, clothing it with skin and flesh and knitting bones and sinews (weight 6.8). Pair score 14.2.

Only in Psalm 139, God's all-knowing presence and the embryo: Darkness is not dark to God; night shines like day, darkness and light are alike; 'YHWH, you have searched me and known me': God knows sitting and rising, thoughts from afar, every word before it is spoken; 'Do I not hate those who hate you, YHWH? I hate them with perfect hatred'; 'If I take the wings of the dawn (shahar) and dwell at the far end of the sea, even there your hand leads me'; No soul dies except by God's leave at a term written (kitaban mu'ajjalan); Speaker was made in secret and embroidered (ruqqamti) in the depths of the earth; No calamity befalls the earth or yourselves but it is in a Book before God brings it into being; Nothing wet or dry but is in a clear book; Fleeing from God, or to God [divergence between the texts]; God's knowledge of a person's thoughts and words, from afar or from near [divergence between the texts]; God knows what the earth diminishes of the dead bodies, and with him is a preserving record; Nowhere to flee God's spirit: if I ascend to heaven you are there, if I make my bed in Sheol you are there; and 14 more.

Only in The resurrection: bones, fingertips and the collarbone: On that day radiant faces look upon their Lord (beatific vision); Does man think he will be left aimless (suda), without purpose or accountability?; Oath by the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwama); At death the soul reaches the collarbones, someone asks 'who is a healer (or charmer, raq)?', leg is wrapped with leg and the drive is to the Lord; The prophet is told not to hasten with the recitation before its revelation is complete; The body of the dead is made whole again, all its limbs complete [divergence between the texts]; An eclipse of the moon as a portent of disaster before which people seek escape or protection [divergence between the texts]; Man will be evidence against himself, even if he offers his excuses; At the prophet's word there is a rattling; bones come together bone to bone, then sinews, flesh and skin cover them, but there is no breath; Then each soul will know what it has brought forward and what it left behind; God created humans (and things) in pairs, male and female; Oath introduced by the negated formula 'No! I swear by...' (la uqsimu / fa-la uqsimu); and 5 more.
